proposedOverrides.summary: A poorly documented third-century Magadha region whose atlas polygon omits its historical heartland and changes to Gupta too early.

fell.text: Around 319 to 320, emerging Gupta rule begins the next separately carded political phase in Magadha.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target magadha-200 is indexed circa 200 to 300 CE and was missing a card and override at initial audit.
Its only geometry is world-200: one Polygon, one ring and 76 positions, bbox 75.361354 to 93.771938 east and 21.017217 to 33.509259 north.
Vaishali, Champa, Varanasi, Kaushambi, Mathura and Tamralipti test inside; Pataliputra, Rajgir, Gaya, Bodh Gaya, Nalanda, Vidisha and Ujjain test outside.
At 300 the same 76-coordinate geometry and hash are relabeled gupta-empire, roughly twenty years before the indexed historical Gupta start in 320.
The 400 Gupta geometry finally contains every tested Magadha center. The map seam is therefore not reliable territorial chronology.
Existing magadha, maurya-empire and gupta-empire cards remain separate; appliesTo is omitted and no shared mapping is changed.
The historical 200 to 300 CE king list is unresolved. Kushan material is real; continuous direct Kushan rule and Murunda rule at Pataliputra remain interpretations.
